page: Microsoft Azure D4als_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine built on the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, delivering clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz within a Microsoft Hyper-V environment. The instance provisions 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is sized at 8.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio that aligns with compute-oriented resource sizing. The CPU architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, complemented by advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, SHA-NI, and VAES.

The instance configuration does not include local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators such as GPUs. All persistent file systems, operating system drives, and operational state must be provisioned through remote network-attached storage volumes, which are supported via Azure premium storage interfaces. Additionally, the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard Azure virtual network routing or external IP assignment for public internet accessibility.

Benchmark assessments highlight strong execution speeds in single-threaded tasks. The D4als_v7 achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests as well as single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression routines. Memory bandwidth reaches 459.17 GB/sec in cached small-block reads and 48.7 GB/sec in uncached large-block reads. Multi-threaded metrics reflect the physical boundary of two underlying cores, placing overall multi-core stress-ng, PassMark CPU scores, and Redis throughput in the average benchmark tier. Large language model inference shows low prompt processing speeds on 7B models, underscoring throughput ceilings in memory-heavy vector operations.

By omitting bundled local NVMe drives and maintaining a lean 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, the D4als_v7 offers an efficient resource profile for CPU-driven tasks that do not require expansive RAM allocations. This setup avoids capital allocation toward underutilized memory. The server is suitable for web serving, stateless microservices, automated build and CI/CD pipelines, and general batch processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D4als_v7 is an x86_64 cloud server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The configuration provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, coupled with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, depending entirely on remote storage for persistent data. Benefiting from modern instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic accelerators like VAES, the CPU delivers top-tier single-core performance and strong single-threaded compression throughput. However, its multi-threaded throughput and large-model prompt processing demonstrate typical mid-range capacity, constrained by the core count. In qualitative terms, the low memory allocation per core optimizes infrastructure spend for CPU-bound tasks that do not demand extensive RAM footprints. It is well suited for web serving, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and stateless computational workloads.
